title: My Flight Was Cancelled

lines.text: SkyWay customer service, Kelly speaking.
Hi, my flight to Dublin has been cancelled, and I need to arrive before Friday for a conference.
I'm sorry about that, Mr Patel. Let me look at your booking. Yes, the flight was cancelled because of a technical problem.
So what can I do?
We can put you on the next flight tomorrow morning, which leaves at seven twenty. You'd arrive in Dublin before nine.
That's fine, but where will I sleep tonight? I'm already at the airport.
The airline will pay for a hotel, and a free taxi will take you there. You'll also receive a voucher for dinner.
How much is the voucher worth?
It's worth twenty pounds, and you can use it at any restaurant in the airport.
Great. Do I need to print a new boarding pass?
No, it will be sent to your phone in a few minutes. If you don't receive it, go to the desk near gate five.
Okay. Thanks for your help.

title: Millbrook Morning Headlines

lines.text: Good morning, Millbrook. It's eight o'clock, and these are the local headlines.
The town council has announced that the old swimming pool will reopen next month after two years of repairs.
That's welcome news. It was closed because the roof was damaged during a storm.
Exactly. The mayor said the new roof had cost a lot, but the pool would be better than before. It will have a children's area and a café.
And what about the price of tickets?
The council says a single ticket will cost three pounds, and children under ten will swim for free.
In other news, roadworks on Bridge Street will start on Monday and will finish in about six weeks.
Drivers are advised to use the ring road, and buses will stop one street away.
Finally, the library is organising a book sale this Saturday. All the money will go to a local animal shelter.
A good reason to clean out your bookshelves!

title: Is This Language App Worth It?

lines.text: Hi everyone, and welcome back to my channel. Today I'm reviewing a language app that I've been using for three months.
First, the good things. The lessons are short, usually about ten minutes, so it's easy to fit them into a busy day.
The app also reminds you to practise, which is very useful if you tend to forget.
Second, it's much cheaper than a private teacher. The monthly price is less than the cost of a single class.
However, there are some problems. The speaking exercises aren't very realistic, because you only repeat sentences, and you never have a real conversation.
Some of the sentences are strange too. Last week, I learned how to say that the elephant is under the table, which I'll probably never need.
My advice is to use the app together with other things, like podcasts and speaking with a friend.
So, would I recommend it? Yes, for beginners, but not for people who already speak the language well.
I'd give it three stars out of five. Thanks for watching, and see you next time!

title: Before We Set Off

lines.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we set off, I'd like to explain a few rules for today's hike.
The walk to the lake is about twelve kilometres, and it should take us about five hours, including a lunch break.
Is the path difficult?
The first part is easy, but the last hour is steep, so you'll need strong boots. Trainers aren't allowed.
What should we carry?
At least two litres of water per person, a waterproof jacket and some food. Weather in the mountains can change quickly.
And if someone feels tired?
Tell me immediately. We'll stop and rest. Nobody has to continue if they don't feel well.
Can we take photos?
Of course, but please stay on the path. Don't leave it to take a photo, because the ground can be slippery.
Are there any animals we should worry about?
Not really. You might see some deer, but they usually run away. Just don't feed them.
One last thing: leave no rubbish behind. If you bring it in, you take it out. Right, let's go!

title: From the Garage to the Stage
focus: Past simple; used to; narrative tenses

lines.text: Today in the studio, we have Eli, the singer of the band Night Owls. Eli, how did the band start?
We met at school. There were four of us, and we used to practise in my uncle's garage every Saturday.
Was it easy at the beginning?
Not at all. Nobody came to our first concert except our parents. I was so nervous that I forgot the words to my own song.
What happened next?
We kept practising, and then a video of one of our songs went around the internet. Suddenly, thousands of people were listening.
How did that feel?
Strange, but wonderful. I couldn't sleep for two nights.
Your new album comes out next month. What's it about?
It's about leaving home and growing up. I wrote most of the songs while I was travelling by train.
Do you have any advice for young musicians?
Don't give up too soon. We played for years before anyone noticed us.
Thanks, Eli, and good luck with the album.

title: My Laptop Won't Turn On

lines.text: TechHelp, Wes speaking. How can I help?
Hello. My laptop won't turn on, and I have an essay due tomorrow morning.
Don't worry, let's try to solve it. First, is the laptop plugged in?
Yes, and I can see a small orange light on the charger.
Okay, that's good. Now, unplug the charger, and hold down the power button for fifteen seconds.
Done. Nothing happened.
Now plug in the charger again, and wait for one minute before pressing the power button once.
Wait a moment... The screen is lighting up! It's working!
Great. If it happens again, repeat the same steps. Has the laptop been dropped recently?
Hmm, my little brother knocked it off the desk last week.
That could be the reason. I'd recommend saving your essay on a memory stick now, just in case.
Good idea. I'll do it straight away. Thanks so much for your help.

title: Graduation Day
focus: Past simple; present perfect; future with will

lines.text: Good afternoon, students, parents and teachers. It's a great pleasure to speak to you on this special day.
Three years ago, you walked into this school feeling nervous, and some of you didn't know anyone.
Since then, you've learned a lot, not only from books, but also from each other.
I remember the football match in the rain, when nobody wanted to go home.
I also remember the winter play, when the lights went out and Sara carried on singing in the dark.
In a few weeks, many of you will be starting new schools, and some will begin working.
You may feel afraid, but remember that you've already done something difficult: you've grown up.
My advice is simple. Be curious, be kind and don't be afraid of making mistakes.
If you fail at something, you'll learn from it, and next time you'll do better.
Please stay in touch with us. Our door will always be open to you.
Congratulations to every one of you, and good luck!
